title: Where to go in New England this August
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Milford Oyster Festival in Connecticut will be held August 14-15, featuring music, food, and oysters at Fowler Field.
A new boutique hotel, The Foreside Inn, opened in Kittery, Maine, offering easy access to shops and restaurants in Maine's oldest downtown.
Dine Out Boston runs from August 1-15, offering multi-course lunch and dinner menus with prices from $27 to $55.

title: Investigation underway after 2 found dead along same stretch of Mass. river
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Authorities investigate two bodies found days apart in the Connecticut River, Western Mass, less than a mile apart.
Hermes Mariano Almonte, 21, drowned near Migratory Way in Turners Falls; no foul play suspected.
Unidentified male found deceased near Smead Island; investigations by State and Montague Police ongoing.

title: Federal investigation finds Burlington schools violated the law over ‘graphic’ student survey
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Burlington Public Schools violated federal law by forcing students to take a survey containing sensitive topics despite parental objections.
The U.S. Department of Education requires the district to provide survey content to parents and update district policies.
The district ceased its contract with the survey vendor and agreed not to issue new surveys until policy changes are approved.

title: Pedestrian struck by vehicle on Cape Cod has died
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A pedestrian in Chatham, struck by a vehicle on Saturday morning, died from injuries sustained in the incident.
The crash occurred at 7:50 a.m. on Route 28 near Crosby Lane, with the driver staying at the scene.
Chatham Police are investigating the collision and have not specified when the pedestrian passed away.

title: Vrabel: Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas is getting closer to participating in training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas is nearing a return to practice after a knee procedure kept him sidelined.
Jacas, a second-round pick, recently signed his rookie contract which includes a knee injury waiver.
Coach Mike Vrabel expects Jacas back before veteran Harold Landry, who is on the PUP list.

title: Wondering how to fit that 48-oz. iced coffee in your car? Don’t worry, Dunkin’ has got you
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: Dunkin' reintroduces its 48-ounce 'Iced Beverage Bucket' with a new cup holder for car use.
The cup holder accessory is priced at $12 and sold out quickly after its release.
The 'Iced Beverage Bucket' will be available again starting August 7 for a limited time.

title: Get the ultimate New England summer travel guide
author: Zipporah Osei
bullets: Boston.com offers 'Summer Six,' a free newsletter with travel tips and activities for Boston and New England.
The newsletter includes curated content on beach towns, Cape Cod activities, and scenic adventures like hikes and camping.
'Summer Six' also highlights popular destinations, dining spots, and hidden gems across Massachusetts and New England.

title: First responders detail scene at Duxbury home on Day 3 of Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Firefighter PJ Hussey testified about chaotic conditions at Lindsay Clancy's Duxbury home during the January 2023 incident.
Paramedics unsuccessfully attempted CPR on the Clancy children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson, and 8-month-old Callan.
Defense claims Lindsay Clancy was battling postpartum mental illness, with an insanity defense being considered.

title: U-Haul data: Where every generation is moving after leaving the Boston area
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: U-Haul's midyear report shows New Hampshire, New York, and Rhode Island as top destinations for Boston-area movers across generations.
Baby Boomers favored New Hampshire and Florida, while Gen X and Millennials showed preference for New York and California.
Massachusetts did not rank in the top 10 net-gain states; Boston experienced the state's largest population decline last year.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (July 30)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: Celine, a French-Canadian restaurant, is set to open in Fort Point in late September.
Jafra Café & Lounge in Inman Square offers Palestinian comfort foods and a vibrant dining experience.
Scrappie's Pizzeria is opening a new location in Beacon Hill by late September or early October.
